_verification_note: Commands assert PROPERTIES this slice's own design contract requires (exact function/grant/revoke shape, exact negative-scope absences), not pinned literals like row/test counts -- same style dd38-dd86-chat-schema-core's manifest uses. Reviewer must verify the test file's negative-proof assertions actually check the denial/RAISE-LOG/exception-message behavior described in the slice doc SS9, not just that a describe/it block with a matching name exists -- in particular (codex round-05 [P2], correcting this note's own prior text, which required the OPPOSITE of what round-04's client_min_messages fix made correct): the RAISE LOG capture test must assert client_min_messages='log' produces ZERO client-visible notice content on every denial path, not that the driver receives the notice -- assert_dm_allowed's own SET client_min_messages=warning clause makes the latter permanently unobservable from any client connection, by design, so a test that still expected to see notice content would itself be proof the leak this migration exists to close had regressed.

security_review.reason: First SECURITY DEFINER surface implementing the DD-55 hard gate for cross-person DM abuse prevention -- the mechanism the entire open-DM feature's safety posture structurally depends on (dd38-dd86-chat-schema-core's own dm_current_read_allowed calls dm_safety_enabled()/chat_pair_blocked() directly). A fail-open bug here (mis-ordered checks, a one-directional block check, a missing REVOKE, or an accidental grant to app) would let a blocked pair evade the block or let PII about denial reasons leak through the generic exception. Security round must specifically verify: dm_safety_enabled() truly fails closed (COALESCE) when the config row is missing; chat_pair_blocked() checks BOTH directions; assert_dm_allowed()'s raised exception text never varies by deny_reason; that app/app_worker/readonly have zero grant on any of the three tables and zero EXECUTE on any of the three functions after migration; and (amended 2026-08-05, hardened codex round-04 [P1]) that the RAISE LOG line fires only when audit_enabled is true and never leaks to ANY client -- assert_dm_allowed's own SET client_min_messages=warning clause must force that threshold for the duration of the call regardless of what the caller's own session requests, closing what was a real client-visible leak in the pre-round-04 design (client_min_messages is a caller-controlled session GUC, not something SECURITY DEFINER alone protects) -- server log only, no table, so no caller-reachable read path of any kind.
